_comment: Byte ceiling and parser cap for the self-hosted hook bundle (dist/hooks/dispatch.js). Registered by road-to-a-hook-bundle-with-one-yaml-reader step 2.1. Read by src/scripts/check_hook_bundle_composition.ts, which builds the bundle from source with --metafile and compares. WHY A CEILING AT ALL: every concern is inlined into one bundle that every hook event loads, so a dependency added for one concern is paid by all of them, on every dispatch. The second YAML parser that opened this roadmap cost 95,846 bytes and reached a release as a review finding rather than as a red check. A ceiling makes the next one a red check.
max_bytes_derivation: Measured 1,514,715 bytes on origin/main at 213d87055 (the gate's own reading, APFS-cloned node_modules so no worktree path artefacts). The ceiling is that reading plus ~2.3 % of headroom, rounded to 1,550,000, on the same doctrine as the 2026-10-01 registration: a bundle is rebuilt from source on every run, so an esbuild minor that renames symbols moves the figure by hundreds of bytes with no change to this tree, and a ceiling one byte above the reading would red on that. Composition is healthy at this reading and was checked rather than assumed: one YAML package (258,833 bytes) and 1,238,525 bytes of own source, so the growth is own code, not a re-entered dependency. The 1,564,211-byte pre-swap regression this roadmap closed still cannot reappear under it. RAISED to 1,550,500 on 2026-10-23 for the InstructionsLoaded binding (237 bytes against 51 of headroom); the reasoning and the measured alternative are the `raise_log` entry whose `to` is 1,550,500, so this paragraph describes the 1,550,000 registration and the raise is recorded there rather than restated.
shrink_only_note: A RAISE needs a recorded reason in `raise_log` below naming what was added and why it could not be avoided. Enforced since road-to-a-ratification-fence-that-follows-its-imports 3.2: the gate reads `max_bytes` at the base revision, and a working value above it fails unless `raise_log` gained an entry whose `to` equals the new value. A lowering needs no entry. This file is also on the ratification gate's watched set, so a raise carries a record as well as a log entry.

raise_log.what_was_added: Nothing in this commit. The 1,500,000 ceiling was red on the very commit that registered it: measured 1,511,489 bytes at 22b19e520, which is the merge of the PR that introduced the budget. Its derivation read 1,469,738 bytes on the PR branch, whose base predated three PRs that had merged meanwhile — the failure-event binding of #2160 (sixteen concerns on a new slot), the touched-file quality pass of #2152, and the evidence classification of #2153 — and #2162 landed after it. The gate ran on each PR's pre-merge tree and never on the merge result, so every one of those PRs was green alone and the trunk was red the moment they were together.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The bytes are deliberately merged capability, not an accident to trim: the composition check above shows one parser and no duplicate dependency, so there is nothing to remove that would not remove a feature. The alternative — reverting a merged lane to fit a ceiling derived against a base that no longer exists — would discard working code to satisfy a number that never described this tree.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Measuring the ceiling against the merge result rather than the PR branch. A ceiling derived on a branch is a statement about that branch; the trunk is what the gate defends, and the two diverge exactly when several lanes land in one day.

raise_log.what_was_added: The queued engine work the 28,000 ceiling was sized for, landed together: the validated identifier rows of one-detector 2.3 (IBAN, card, e-mail with a keyed-digest allowlist, three phone shapes, German tax id, US SSN), and three free-tier credential rows (Hugging Face, NVIDIA, Replicate) of free-hands 1.2. The invisible-character normalisation of one-detector 2.5 (`egress_normalize.ts`) is not in this chunk: the engine does not import it (corrected 2026-10-23, road-to-a-tick-the-shipped-path-earns 1.4). Measured 30,445 bytes when the raise landed; 30,493 bytes at the ratified revision, after the round-6 IBAN rows.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Each addition is an identifier or credential detection row; the 2026-10-18 derivation already counted them as the chunk's planned growth and underestimated their sum by about 2.4 KB. The chunk is loaded only when a caller needs detection, so no dispatch pays these bytes; the dispatch bundle itself is unchanged.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Re-measuring the queued items' sum when the ceiling was set, rather than estimating each.

raise_log.what_was_added: The `InstructionsLoaded` binding: one `LAZY_CONCERNS` row for the observer (its 11,097-byte body ships in its own chunk, never in this bundle) and the event name in the three vocabularies the bundle carries (dispatcher, collector, journal). Measured 1,550,186 bytes with the binding by the gate; the same esbuild invocation on the base and on this branch differs by 237 bytes, so the base sat at 1,549,949 — 51 bytes of headroom.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: D8 (council, 2026-10-18) asked for room before a raise. Room was tried and measured: moving `session-eol` (27,708 B in-bundle, `stop` alone) into a chunk freed 29,948 B (same esbuild invocation, with and without the move) but produced a 259,330-byte chunk (`yaml` external) required on every `stop` — about 8.5 times the bytes that event parses today, to buy 186. The observer itself was already moved out. What remains in the bundle is the row and three event-name strings, which no chunk can carry.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the base sat 51 bytes under the ceiling, so any new event in the vocabulary would have tripped it. Sized to this binding plus about 300 bytes; step 3.3's promotion is sized when it is built.

raise_log.by: agent, feat/code-graph-auto-refresh (PR #2604) merged onto docs/inbox-2026-10-ac-roadmap (PR #2603) on the owner's instruction to target #2603
raise_log.what_was_added: One `LAZY_CONCERNS` row for the `code-graph-refresh` session concern (its 12,726-byte body ships in its own chunk). Each branch fit alone: #2603 measured 1,550,498 B, #2604 added 153 B to a base that sat 356 B under. Merged, the gate measured 1,550,617 B — 117 over. With the `provider_id` type check restored in validate.ts (the one #2603 had dropped for its last 2 bytes, asked for by both ratification seats of round 12) the final combined measurement is 1,550,751 B, 249 under the new ceiling.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Room was tried and measured, as D8 asks: moving `handoff-context` (10,433 B in-bundle, `session_start` alone) into a chunk would free about 10 KB but produces a 581,613-byte chunk inlined, 319,233 bytes with `yaml` external — required on every `session_start` to buy 117 bytes, the same trade the 2026-10-23 entry refused for `session-eol`. Shortening the row's strings saves under 20 bytes. What remains is the row, which no chunk can carry. Sized to the merged measurement plus about 380 bytes.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Measuring the two branches together before the merge: two lanes that each fit a ceiling with a few hundred bytes to spare do not fit it together, and #2603 had already spent its last 2 bytes by dropping a provider_id type check in validate.ts.

raise_log.what_was_added: A user-addressed channel in the dispatcher: a `notification` concern may reply `user_notice`, and on claude the dispatcher emits it as `systemMessage`, the field the host documents as shown to the user and not added to model context (hooks/user_notice.ts: collectUserNotice; host_semantics: withUserNotice, which merges context, the native emission and the notice as structures and falls back to the old output whenever a field it would extend has the wrong type, and writeStdout, which writes the output and only then a small user-global receipt naming the session and the notice id for each notice actually in the output, so a concern counts a notice as shown only on that receipt). Plus one LAZY_CONCERNS row for `update-notice`, whose body ships in its own chunk. Measured with one esbuild invocation over origin/main and over this branch after merging it: +2,945 bytes of own source (host_semantics +1,582, user_notice +1,095, dispatch_hook +116, lazy_concern +152; identifier renames elsewhere net 0), so 1,553,708 B against 1,551,000, the base reading 1,550,763. The logic sits in the two helper modules rather than in dispatch_hook.ts because that file is at the 1,500-line source cap. The first measurement, +1,391 B, predated the structural merge, the type guards and the delivery receipt that council rounds asked for.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The channel is what step 3.1 was reopened for: every host runs the dispatcher on pipes, so a notice on stderr reached nobody, and a council round refused the registration for exactly that. The bytes are dispatcher code on the emission path of every event, so a chunk cannot carry them; the concern body is already in one. Room was not re-tried: the 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24 entries measured the two narrow-event chunk candidates (`session-eol`, `handoff-context`) as buying a few hundred bytes for a quarter-megabyte require on every event, and nothing in this tree has changed that trade. Own code was compacted first (1,545 -> 1,391 B).
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the base sat about 240 bytes under the ceiling. Sized to this change plus 292 bytes.

raise_log.what_was_added: The invisible-character normalisation of one-detector 2.5 wired into the engine: `replaceValues` and `tallyText` now detect through `egress_normalize.ts` (`detectWithExtent`), and a rule's extent reader (`through`) runs on the normalised text with its end mapped back, so a key block whose BEGIN and END markers both carry a zero-width character is removed whole instead of refused or left behind. Measured 30,511 bytes on origin/main, 31,907 with the wiring alone, 32,305 with the extent fix.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The 2026-10-18 derivation queued this rescan inside the 32,000 ceiling and the 2026-10-22 raise recorded it as not yet in the chunk. Room was taken first: `LATIN_TWIN` moved out of confusables.ts as a hex-encoded string pair so the chunk no longer carries that module's four script regexes, and the normaliser keeps one origin array instead of two (32,670 down to 31,907). The extent fix that a council seat found in round 1 of the ratification review adds about 400 bytes of mapping code no smaller form carries. The chunk loads only when a caller needs detection; the dispatch bundle is unchanged.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Measuring the wired engine when 2.5 was first built rather than the unwired module, and a disguised-marker key block in the extent tests from the start.

raise_log.what_was_added: Two things, measured per module from one esbuild metafile over origin/main and over this branch. (1) One `LAZY_CONCERNS` row for `layer-promote` (+144 B); its body, the thin pass and the ownership-ledger rewrite ship in their own 54,058-byte chunk. (2) `projectTreeForm()`, the project tree's precedence rule, now on the live path (+793 B to `project_tree_form.ts`): before, it had no caller and esbuild dropped it, which is exactly the defect the full-quorum council of 2026-10-24 named for step 3.6. Gate reading 1,554,423 B against 1,554,000.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: D10 recorded that 3.3 would need more than the bytes left and asked for the next raise or extraction to be sized from all blocked work then; 3.3 and 3.6 are that work. Room was not re-tried: the 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24 entries measured both narrow-event chunk candidates (`session-eol`, `handoff-context`) as buying a few hundred bytes for a quarter-megabyte require on every event, and nothing has changed that trade. The 793 B are the precedence rule itself, which the projector's path must carry, and the 144 B are the row no chunk can carry.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the base sat about 514 bytes under the ceiling. Sized to this change plus 377 bytes. Re-measured on the merge with #2635 (`subagent-constraints`, +159 B on main without a raise): 1,554,582 B, still under this ceiling, so no further raise.

raise_log.what_was_added: The user's own instruction layer in the subagent-constraints digest: `<config dir>/CLAUDE.md`, the files it imports one level deep, and every rule under `<config dir>/rules/` carried by its Iron Law blocks, with a fixed priority (the first law block of each safety-floor and consequence-class rule first, its later blocks listed as cut, then the project files, the user files and the other rules), a grouped rules inventory, and the shared `_lib/rule_law_section` reader for where a law section ends. Measured 12,194 bytes on the base and 23,843 with the change. The ratification rounds added whole-entry inventories, canonical floor-rule reads, import deduplication by real path, a count-only reservation ahead of the floor laws, and whole-or-nothing placement of each floor rule's first law block with room kept to name any floor rule left out.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The owner kept #2639 open until a skipping worker also receives the user layer, so the code has to ship in this chunk, which is the only carrier on the host's SubagentStart path. Reusing `rule_law_section` instead of a second law-extent parser costs bytes but keeps one definition of a law section across the projector, the lint and this concern. The chunk loads only on claude `subagent_start`; the dispatch bundle is unchanged.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Scoping step 2.4's carrier against the 2026-10-22 probe, which already showed the skip dropping the user rule layer, instead of against the project CLAUDE.md files alone.

raise_log.what_was_added: `readEgressMode` resolves the egress mode from one read of the settings layers, merged in the cascade's order, instead of reading the layers and then running the full settings cascade, which read them again. Ratified 2/2 in round 6 (agents/evidence/ratifications/inbox-2026-10-al-am-egress.md). Measured with the change: 1,554,922 B; origin/main at bead1e828 alone: 1,554,745 B, so the change adds 177 B against 55 B of headroom that main's own star-ask work left. The new ceiling is that reading plus exactly the 55 B of headroom main had (1,554,922 + 55 = 1,554,977), so the change takes no margin beyond its own bytes.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Five ratification rounds removed every cheaper design: a block-only reader that parsed less than the whole layer, and a per-layer skip that judged on one read and resolved on another, were both refused, and the read-once-per-path reduction the last refusal asked for is part of these bytes. Inlining the function into its only caller was measured and saves 67 B, still 55 B over, at the cost of a deeper body. The change removes about 16 ms cold and 6.6 ms warm from every hook event on an installed project.

raise_log.what_was_added: The owner's 2026-10-22 quota directive on the dispatch path: one LAZY_CONCERNS row shared by `quota-notice` and `metered-spawn-ask` (both bodies live in their own chunk), `permission_gate` emitting a concern's `ask` vote as the host's native ask with its reason, and `_lib/pressure_state` — a ten-line reader of the plan-window verdict the status-line tap leaves behind — used by `delegation-nudge` (no fan-out push into a hot window) and `spawn-guard-shadow` (`plan_window: would_wait`). Measured 1,556,562 B with the change on a base of 1,554,827 B, after ratification rounds 1 and 2 restricted the host ask to `effect: confirmation` concerns, passed that effect from the dispatcher and bounded the reasons. The ceiling, 1,556,670 B, was set at the round-1 reading (1,556,520 B) plus the 150 B of headroom the base had; 108 B remain.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Room was made first and measured: compacting the LAZY_CONCERNS table and dropping `path.join` from its rows freed 202 B, which carried the shared row and the ask passthrough with 16 B to spare. The two dispatch-path consumers could not follow: reading the ledger and the pressure model there cost 4,984 B, so the model moved to the tap (a CLI process, outside this bundle) and the consumers read its verdict file instead. What remains is the verdict reader and two call sites, which no chunk can carry because both concerns are in-bundle.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the base sat 150 bytes under the ceiling, so any in-bundle consumer of a new state file would have tripped it.

raise_log.what_was_added: One `LAZY_CONCERNS` row for `intake-pass`, the owner-chosen OQ-25 concern on `user_prompt_submit` (every host that binds the slot): on a task prompt it injects one line naming the intake pass, and its body ships in its own 9,807-byte chunk. Measured by the gate: 1,556,763 B with the row on a base of 1,556,669 B, so +94 B for the row; the ceiling is that reading plus the 1 B of headroom the base had.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The base sat 1 B under the ceiling, so no concern can be added without either a raise or a removal elsewhere. The concern was built in-bundle first and measured at +2,930 B; moving its body into a lazy chunk cut that to the 94-byte row, which is the smallest form the dispatcher can reach a new concern in. Making room by compacting another module would change code this decision does not own.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the owner chose a shipped, default-on concern on 2026-10-28, and any shipped concern costs at least its LAZY_CONCERNS row.

raise_log.what_was_added: The self-repair user-report detector on the dispatch path: one combined recurrence pattern (ordinal + punctuation, `wie oft noch ich`, `how many times do I`, `as I mentioned before`, `told you this`, `immer noch nicht`, an addressed `schon wieder`) under which 6 of the 10 trigger phrases `recurring-criticism` names fire and the other 4 are allowlisted with a reason (each needs a contextual constraint), plus a `subject` capture kept out of the tested outgoing paths (`tabs`) that makes counting repeats by subject possible; the counter itself is not built here (later/road-to-a-noted-that-is-a-write 1.2). Measured 1,557,828 B on a base of 1,556,650 B (origin/main 965c4db02 with its own self_repair.ts, same gate run): +1,178 B; the ceiling leaves 72 B. Where the subject goes was probed, not asserted: rendering it into the upstream body turned both `payload-has-only-closed-fields` tests (tests/scripts/self_repair_release.test.ts, which check the whole outgoing release payload and the fallback issue body) red, and feeding it into `fingerprint()` turned `is not part of the fingerprint` (tests/scripts/self_repair.test.ts) red; both passed once restored.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Room was made first and measured: the new patterns were merged into one alternation and the narrower `how many times (do|must|should) i` pattern, now subsumed, was removed (growth 1,274 B -> 1,128 B); the first-person precision fix the council asked for then added 50 B, for 1,178 B final. The detector runs in the `self-repair` concern on `user_prompt_submit`, which is inlined, not a lazy chunk; moving it into a chunk is a dispatcher change larger than this raise. The subject ships now because road-to-a-correction-that-is-heard AC-2 requires the record to name what a repeated correction was about. Re-based onto the 2026-10-28 intake-pass raise; ratified by AI council 2026-10-29 (agents/evidence/ratifications/hook-bundle-raise-20261029.md).

raise_log.what_was_added: Measured with this gate's own build (APFS-cloned node_modules) on the branch merged with origin/main 14012757d: 1,560,119 B against 1,557,828 B for origin/main itself, so +2,291 B; the ceiling leaves 281 B of headroom, the jitter margin this file's own doctrine names. Per module (metafile bytesInOutput, branch minus base): concern_timings.ts +593 (per-dispatch max RSS and CPU microseconds, read only when the timings sink is armed), stop_snapshot.ts +563 and end_review_nudge_hook.ts +282 (one git numstat / untracked read per Stop dispatch shared by end-review-nudge and obligation-settle, which removes a second `git diff` and `git ls-files` spawn from every Stop), compile_cache.ts +500 and dispatch_entry.ts +114 (node compile cache for the lazy concern chunks, fail-open), host_rate_marker_hook.ts +100 (one set naming which host failure classes park a run). No git-authorization or other guard code changes: an earlier revision of this raise carried a pending-refusal exception there, which the 2026-10-31 council round refused and which was withdrawn.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Room was made first and measured: the first build was +5,050 B, because the park marker's reset time was looked up inside the hook and pulled the quota ledger and pressure model into the bundle; that lookup moved to run_supervise (a CLI, outside the bundle), the marker field became dead code and was removed, the failure-class table became a one-entry set, and the withdrawn git-authorization exception went with its bytes (+5,050 -> +2,291 B). What remains is new behaviour on the dispatch path itself: the Stop memo has to live where both Stop concerns run, the compile cache has to be enabled by the entry that loads the lazy chunks, and the resource sample has to be taken by the process whose usage it reports. The base had 72 B of headroom, so none of it fits without a raise.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: This gate, on the first push; it did, and the reduction above is the response.

raise_log.what_was_added: The turn-end binding of the code-graph-refresh concern and the bounds eight ratification rounds required: a `git rev-parse HEAD` probe; a claim file per (HEAD, THROTTLE_MS window) in a per-UTC-day folder, created with O_EXCL right before the spawn after an age check by a fresh clock; a sweep of day folders two or more days old; containment that refuses a claim unless every path component from the repository root down is a real directory (lstat); tracked claim storage refused; the hook slot in the outcome record. Measured 19,741 bytes; ceiling 20,500 leaves about 4 %.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The owner reported on 2026-11-01 a project map 20 commits behind; bound on session_start alone, a long session never refreshes. Without the throttle a turn-end binding would spawn a node process per turn, which is the waste the 2026-10-23 council kept it off `stop` for. The chunk loads only for this concern, so no other dispatch pays the bytes.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the growth is the feature.

raise_log.what_was_added: The `code-graph-refresh` row on the `stop` slot of seven platforms in the compiled manifest, and the opt-out marker path in the shared graph-home resolver. Measured 1,561,506 bytes, 1,106 over the 1,560,400 ceiling.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: A binding is a manifest row the dispatch bundle carries; the concern body itself stays in its own chunk. The resolver field is the single place a layout path is chosen (check_graph_writers), so the opt-out cannot live elsewhere.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the growth is the feature.

raise_log.what_was_added: Profile awareness on the session-register path, which runs on session_start: `session_profile` in `_lib/session_register.ts` (reads only the environment) plus `install/agentSwitchProfile.ts` (2,033 B), newly pulled into the bundle so the profile is parsed by the one existing matching rule rather than a second copy; and `_lib/provider_home.ts` (903 B), the single resolver for `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `CODEX_HOME` that `claude_plugin.claude_config_dir` now delegates to. Measured 1,566,892 bytes by the gate, 4,892 over the 1,562,000 ceiling; the base sat at 1,561,506.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Room was looked for first: `sessions_cli.ts` (16,380 B) rides in through `env_session_id` and `other_worktree_branches_detailed`, but extracting those is an unrelated refactor of two hooks and a CLI; the schema-flag code added to it is tree-shaken because the bundled entry never reaches `cmd_list`. Inlining a reduced agent-switch path match would save about 1.5 KB at the cost of a second matching rule that drifts from the first. The profile must be recorded when the session registers, in the hook, because a later reader runs in another process with another environment.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the growth is the feature. Sized to the measurement plus about 500 bytes of rebuild jitter.

raise_log.what_was_added: The strike ledger on the verification recorder's post_tool_use path: `_lib/strike_ledger.ts` (signature normalisation, the SAME/NEW/FIXED/FLAKY fold over per-agent edit counters, TTL expiry and size caps, with every edit counter a surviving entry depends on kept, and an allowlist rebuild of every persisted entry) and `_lib/strike_ledger_io.ts` (non-blocking locked write of agents/state/strike-ledger.json, fed the run the recorder appended), 8,898 B. The gate measured 1,578,313 bytes; the base at b234d08480 measured 1,569,415 here, 2,015 over the 1,567,400 ceiling before this change. That base overage is the growth merged between the 2026-11-02 raise (47161a7b70, measured 1,566,892) and b234d08480: +2,523 B from the non-merge commits in that range touching bundled sources — 7742bad8c4, 5dbafe73c5, 850c3619eb, dcb61c6f98 (provider-home and profile fixes) and e8ee59465f, 8afea9f246, e00a48598f — none of which carried a raise_log entry.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The ledger has to observe the run in the same hook invocation that records it: the recorder clears its runs at every turn boundary, which is the defect the ledger exists to outlive, so a later reader in another process would see nothing. A lazy chunk would need its own manifest concern (+1 on the concern_count ratchet) and a second stdin parse of the same event for 8 KB. The base overage is included rather than left red, because a ceiling below the trunk's own reading fails every branch cut from it.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: For the base overage: measuring the ceiling on the merge result, as the first raise_log entry already says. For the ledger: nothing earlier — the growth is the feature. Sized to the final measurement (1,578,313) plus 287 bytes of rebuild jitter.

raise_log.what_was_added: The hardening the Phase 4 ratification rounds asked for, all in `_lib/switch_relay.ts`: a back-off that rests the link for the session after three unanswered calls in a row until the next reset and says so once (7.1); a `done` record kept until the Stop path has checkpointed it, with an outcome-told flag so it is still reported once (7.3); a per-record expiry (the request's expiresAt plus a day, at most seven days) and a locked read-modify-write so a prompt relay and a Stop checkpoint running at once neither undo each other's flag nor revive a deleted record (7.5). Council round 1 (agents/evidence/council/agent-switch-hardening-ratification-r1-20261108.question.md) refused it and named defects that were then fixed in the same chunk: a kept `done` record could be replaced by a later raise; the checkpoint and the relayed line were claimed after their side effect, so two Stops or two prompts could both act; the back-off file was unlocked; a stale-lock breaker could have its successor's lock removed by the slow holder; a successful probe did not count as an answer; abandoned state files were never pruned. Round 2 (…-r2-20261108.question.md) refused it for one defect, also fixed here: a checkpoint reservation was stored as completion, so a prompt could forget a `done` record while its write was still pending, and a write that threw or a Stop that died left the obligation lost; that was fixed by separating reservation from completion. Round 3 (…-r3-20261108.question.md) refused on edge cases of that reservation (a completion update that misses the lock, a slow holder clearing its successor's reservation) and on expiry dropping an owed checkpoint; the strategy changed instead of adding more locking: the checkpoint is one file per run replaced atomically (run_checkpoint.ts writeCheckpoint), so the guarantee is at least once and the reservation was removed; an expired record gets one last Stop that writes a checkpoint still owed; a present discovery no longer resets the failure count. Round 4 (…-r4-20261108.question.md) refused on that expiry look forgetting a record whose last write failed, whose lookup got no answer, or while the link rested; such a record is now kept until nothing is owed, bounded by the eight-day prune, which a session blocked by one now also runs. Anthropic's seat also refused the raise itself as a threshold the implementer moves; openai's seat disagreed. Round 5 (…-r5-20261108.question.md) refused on ordering: two Stops writing at once could leave an older snapshot over a newer one; the checkpoint is now built and written while the record lock is held, and a Stop that finds it completed meanwhile does not write. Neither seat held the raise itself as a dealbreaker in round 5. Measured 47,287 B against 39,584 B on origin/main 12bd765ce1, both built with this gate's own `buildChunk`; ceiling 49,400 B leaves 2,113 B, about 4 % of the reading. Latency with the link answering, failing, hanging, resting and absent, and the rollback criterion, are in agents/evidence/metrics/agent-switch-link-latency-20261108.md.

LOWERED to 29,900 on 2026-11-10 (road-to-a-link-with-agent-switch 8.4): the agent-switch link moved into its own chunk, src/scripts/switch_link.ts, which this one loads only while the switch question is on, through `hooks/lazy_load.ts` rather than the lazy-concern table; measured 27,162 bytes after the move against 47,877 before it, and the ceiling is that reading plus about 10 %, rounded; 27,128 bytes once the record lock rewrite left this change for its own (council round 5 asked to review the lock separately).

Measured 27,500 bytes on 2026-11-10 (road-to-a-link-with-agent-switch 8.4), with the record lock as on main: council round 5 asked to review the lock rewrite separately, so it left this change (29,329 B with it). The chunk holds the agent-switch link: the prompt's switch turn (raise, relay, back-off) and the Stop path's checkpoint, with the record and its lock (`_lib/switch_relay.ts`), the link's spawn (`_lib/agent_switch_link.ts`, `_lib/spawn_env.ts`) and the atomic writer. No `yaml`. The ceiling is that reading plus about 10 %, rounded, the margin of the quota_notice and self_repair rows. WHY IT IS A CHUNK: in the quota_notice chunk the link took that chunk to 47,877 B against a 41,000 B ceiling a ratification never accepted raising (Phase 7, rounds 1-6 refused); the switch question is opt-in (D5), so a prompt without it should not parse the link at all. `quota-notice` loads `switchTurn` from here only when the question is on, and the Stop path loads `checkpointBeforeMove` only for a session with a switch record. A missing or mis-digested chunk means no switch question and no checkpoint before a move, the same as running without agent-switch; a checkpoint already owed stays owed for the next Stop. WHAT IT COSTS: a prompt without the opt-in, the default, parses 27,128 B instead of 47,877 B; a prompt with it parses both chunks, 54,628 B instead of 47,877 B (+6,751 B, +14 %): the loader (`hooks/lazy_load.ts` and `hooks/bundle_digest.ts`, about 2,600 B), helpers both chunks carry (`_lib/user_global_paths.ts`, part of `_lib/quota_ledger.ts`, about 1,600 B), and the call-surface code. The two ceilings add up to 60,200 B; the chunk group `agent-switch-link-opted-in` bounds the two together at 60,100 B.

Measured 9,807 bytes on 2026-10-28 (the intake-pass concern, its task-prompt and question predicates after council round 1, and the shared `isSyntheticPrompt` reader), no `yaml`. The ceiling is that reading plus about 10 %, rounded, with no growth queued. Bound on `user_prompt_submit` on every host that binds the slot; the dispatch bundle carries only its LAZY_CONCERNS row. A missing chunk falls back to the spawn path and costs latency, never the line.

Measured 18,792 bytes on 2026-11-08 (the compact-checkpoint concern: a keys-only marker in the user-global runtime directory with an inspection-bounded, complete sweep of abandoned markers, its bounded non-following reader, and the containment check and runtime-path helpers it reuses), `yaml` external. The ceiling is that reading plus about 10 %, rounded, with no growth queued. Bound on `pre_compact` and `session_start` on claude only; the dispatch bundle carries only its LAZY_CONCERNS row.

Measured 13,287 bytes on 2026-11-02: rows 2.1 and 2.2, already in the hook Finding shape, of check_web_launch_readiness (third-party load on first paint, superseded statute on a legal page), the 12-row provider register and the one-row supersession table. Loaded by design_pass_hook only for an .html/.css write. The ceiling is the next thousand above that reading; the 713-byte (5.4 %) margin is what that rounding leaves, not a growth estimate. A register row serialises to 150-223 bytes (mean 181), so the margin admits about three more rows before the chunk must be re-measured and this row re-derived.

Measured 55,991 bytes on 2026-11-04 for the roadmap agents/roadmaps/archive/road-to-a-noted-that-is-a-write.md. The chunk holds the self-repair concern, its four detectors including persistence-claim, the record store with the target and subject indexes, and the Class-A telemetry shadow (emitDefectShadow: a structural-fields-only copy of a queued record for the org telemetry pack, inert unless that pack activated telemetry); `yaml` is external, resolved from the installed package as for the chat_history, update_notice and star_ask chunks. The ceiling is that reading plus about 10 %, rounded, the same margin as the quota_notice and intake_pass rows. The margin approves no planned code: a later addition to the chunk is measured and reviewed on its own change. WHY IT WAS MOVED: the dispatch bundle sat 14 bytes under its 1,582,000 ceiling at origin/main b53718de2 (measured 1,581,986 B by this gate with APFS-cloned node_modules), and the roadmap's detector work had to land somewhere. The concern built alone was 51,156 bytes before the work; moving it out, as the 2026-10-18 council chose for this situation, took the dispatch bundle to 1,557,293 B (-24,693 B, the rest being modules other concerns still import) instead of raising the dispatch ceiling. Bound on `user_prompt_submit` and `stop`; the bundle carries only its LAZY_CONCERNS row. A missing or mis-digested chunk falls back to spawning the same script, which is slower; tests/hooks/self_repair_lazy_paths.test.ts pins that the loader path and the spawn fallback write the same record, and that the built dispatcher falls back to the spawn exactly once with the chunk missing. On either path a failure of the concern does not reject the hook event (`fail_closed: false`, unchanged by this move); the dispatcher still writes that run's exit code to agents/runtime/state/.dispatcher/<session>/self-repair.json, which is where a failing concern is visible.

Registered at 16,523 bytes on 2026-11-08 (15,080 before ratification round 1 replaced the segmenter with a quote-, escape-, comment- and heredoc-aware lexer); raised to 20,600 after ratification round 6 measured 18,774 bytes, and to 22,000 after round 15 measured 20,607 bytes; both raises and what was added are the raise_log entries naming this chunk; the raise and what was added are the raise_log entry naming this chunk for road-to-a-reference-that-arrives-before-the-act. The chunk holds the reference duty: the router walk with trigger_matches, the rule-frontmatter parse, the act-reference table and the shell-act recogniser; `yaml` is external, resolved from the installed package as for the chat_history chunk. The ceiling was the registered reading plus about 10 %, rounded, the margin of the quota_notice, intake_pass and self_repair rows. WHY IT IS A CHUNK: adding the act-time duty in the dispatch bundle measured 1,588,246 B against the 1,585,000 B ceiling (real node_modules install); the duty runs only on a file write or on a Bash command containing a bound act word (`reference_duty_loader.ACT_WORDS`), so it does not belong in the bytes every hook event loads. The bundle keeps the loader, the act-word pre-check and `_lib/ledger_key.ts`. A missing or mis-digested chunk makes the hook count a duty error instead of observing; the guard's read ledger and advisories are unaffected.

chunks_note: A chunk is loaded only when a caller needs it, so its bytes are not paid by every dispatch; its ceiling exists so that the move out of dispatch.js stays a measured place rather than an unmeasured one. The gate builds each chunk with the exact esbuild segment `build:hook-chunks` uses for its entry.

chunk_groups.name: agent-switch-link-opted-in
chunk_groups.derivation: What a prompt with the switch question on parses: the quota_notice chunk and the switch_link chunk it loads. Measured 54,628 bytes together on 2026-11-10 (27,128 + 27,500), against 47,877 bytes for quota_notice alone when it carried the link (+6,751 B, +14 %): the chunk loader with its digest check (`hooks/lazy_load.ts`, `hooks/bundle_digest.ts`, about 2,600 B), helpers both chunks carry (about 1,600 B), and the call-surface code the ratification rounds of the split asked for; the record lock rewrite, 56,491 B with it, left for its own change after council round 5. The ceiling is that reading plus about 10 %, rounded, below the 63,500 B a council seat named as acceptable if the gate enforces it (agents/evidence/council/agent-switch-link-chunk-ratification-r3-20261110.question.md). A prompt without the opt-in parses quota_notice alone, which its own ceiling bounds.

chunk_groups_note: A chunk group bounds the summed bytes of chunks one caller loads together, so a feature split across chunks cannot grow in total while each part stays under its own ceiling. Each named chunk keeps its own ceiling; a group raise needs a raise_log entry whose `chunk_group` is the group's name, by the chunk rule.
max_yaml_packages_note: The dispatch path reads YAML for the hook manifest, the host-lowering table and the settings contract. One reader covers all three. Two cost 95,846 bytes for a single call site and were invisible until an external rescore counted them — which is why this is a cap rather than prose. The package set the cap counts over is YAML_PACKAGES in the gate.
what_this_does_not_bound: Latency. A smaller bundle is not a measured speed-up; src/config/hook-latency-budget.json owns the wall-clock axis and is not derived from this file. Nor does it bound dist/install/install.mjs or dist/mcp/server.mjs, which carry their own module graphs.
